input: The applicator must maintain a 30-meter buffer zone from the nearest pond while spraying the pesticide.
The pesticide must not contaminate ponds or other surface water because of runoff from treated fields.
The operator must stop applying the pesticide when wind speed exceeds the specified limit.
The pesticide must not be used when conditions could cause unacceptable harm to nearby wildlife.
The applicator must observe the required re-entry interval before allowing workers to enter the treated field.
Workers must not be exposed to pesticide residues that could cause harmful health effects.
The operator must wear the required protective equipment while applying the pesticide.
Workers handling the concentrated pesticide must wear chemical-resistant gloves to prevent exposure.
The manufacturer must obtain regulatory authorization before selling the pesticide.
The manufacturer must submit annual sales information to the regulatory authority.
The company must renew the pesticide registration before its authorization expires.
The company must notify the authority of a significant change in the quantity of pesticide distributed.
People exposed to the pesticide must receive appropriate medical treatment for poisoning symptoms.
The pesticide must not cause unacceptable harm to fish or other aquatic organisms.
Handlers must wash contaminated skin immediately after accidental pesticide exposure.
Pesticide use must be managed to prevent contamination of groundwater and surrounding ecosystems.
